knowledge-base.overview: Actix-web 4+ guardrails, type-safe extractors, thin handlers, shared state patterns, custom middleware, error handling, and testing for high-performance Rust web APIs. Loaded automatically when agents work on .rs files importing actix-web.

core-principles.principle: Use extractors (web::Json, web::Path, web::Query) for all request data. Never manually parse HttpRequest unless accessing headers or extensions.
Handlers extract request data and delegate to services. No business logic in handler functions.
Implement ResponseError trait for all custom error types. Never return raw strings from error paths.
Application state is injected via web::Data, never via globals. web::Data wraps state in Arc internally.
Authentication, logging, CORS, and rate limiting belong in middleware, not in handlers.

guardrail.rule: Never perform blocking I/O in async handlers. Actix-web workers run on a Tokio-compatible runtime; blocking starves other requests. Use web::block() for blocking operations.
Implement ResponseError trait for all custom error types. Return structured JSON error bodies — never expose internal details (SQL errors, panic messages) to clients.
Never hardcode secrets (database URL, JWT secret) in source code or Cargo.toml. Load from environment variables via the config crate.
Validate all input extracted from JSON, forms, and path parameters. Use the validator crate with #[derive(Validate)] on request structs. Call .validate() explicitly in handlers.
Set a JSON payload size limit to prevent abuse. Use .app_data(web::JsonConfig::default().limit(1_048_576)) (1 MB default).
Apply middleware at the scope level, not per-route. Use web::scope("/protected").wrap(AuthMiddleware) to protect route groups.
Keep AppState immutable. Wrap in web::Data (Arc-backed). Use tokio::sync::RwLock only if mutation is genuinely required — document why.
Use actix-cors with explicit allowed origins in production. Never use allow_any_origin() in production — it bypasses CORS protection.
Call .into_inner() to unwrap extractors before passing data to service methods. Services should receive plain types, not actix-web extractor wrappers.

project-structure.description: Layered Rust project: entry point bootstraps server, business logic in services, data access in repositories.
project-structure.example: myproject/ ├── Cargo.toml ├── src/ │ ├── main.rs # Server bootstrap: config, pool, routes, HttpServer │ ├── config.rs # Config struct loaded from environment │ ├── routes.rs # Route registration via ServiceConfig │ ├── handlers/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ ├── users.rs # User-related handlers │ │ └── health.rs # Health check endpoint │ ├── models/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── user.rs # Domain models + DTOs with validation │ ├── services/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── user_service.rs # Business logic layer │ ├── repositories/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── user_repository.rs # Database access layer (sqlx) │ ├── middleware/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── auth.rs # Transform + Service auth middleware │ └── errors/ │ ├── mod.rs │ └── app_error.rs # AppError enum + ResponseError impl ├── tests/ │ └── integration_tests.rs └── migrations/

dependencies.example:
[dependencies] actix-web = "4" actix-rt = "2" actix-cors = "0.7" serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] } serde_json = "1.0" sqlx = { version = "0.7", features = ["runtime-tokio", "postgres", "uuid", "chrono"] } validator = { version = "0.16", features = ["derive"] } thiserror = "1.0" anyhow = "1.0" tracing = "0.1" tracing-actix-web = "0.7" uuid = { version = "1.0", features = ["v4", "serde"] } chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] } dotenvy = "0.15" config = "0.14"
[dev-dependencies] actix-rt = "2"

routing.description: Organize routes with web::scope and ServiceConfig for modular registration.

handlers.description: Thin handlers: use .into_inner() on extractors, delegate to service, return AppResult.

error-handling.description: Implement ResponseError trait. Log internal errors server-side; return sanitized messages to clients.

middleware.description: Actix-web middleware uses the Transform + Service trait pair.

rules.rule: Use test::init_service to create a test App instance with the same routes and state
Use test::TestRequest builders to construct requests
Assert on status codes, response bodies, and headers
Use a separate test database provisioned via Testcontainers

quick-reference.item: Thin: extract → .into_inner() → service → HttpResponse; no business logic
web::Data<AppState> (Arc-backed); clone in HttpServer closure; immutable preferred
web::Json, web::Path, web::Query, web::Data, HttpRequest; validate after extraction
web::scope for grouping; .wrap(middleware) at scope level; ServiceConfig for modularity
ResponseError trait; log internal errors; sanitize client messages; AppResult type alias
Transform + Service traits; store auth user in request extensions; .wrap() bottom-to-top
allow_any_origin() in dev only; explicit allowed_origin() in production
actix_web::test module; test::init_service + TestRequest; separate test DB
sqlx::PgPool connection pooling; middleware::Compress; set JSON payload limits; workers(num_cpus::get())
